questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Function on Which to Apply a Root-Finding Method When Applying the Trapezoidal Method
questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=4{x}^{2}y,\,y(0)=1
$$

Using the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx=0.5,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step. Which of the following is the **general form** of $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ in terms of the new values ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and ${y}_{\text{new}},$ and the current values $x$ and $y?$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In this example, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4{x}^{2}y+4({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}{y}_{\text{new}})\cdot 0.5 \\  & ={x}^{2}y+({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+{x}^{2}y+({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}{y}_{\text{new}},\end{aligned}
$$

and moving all terms to the left-hand side gives the equation

$$
{{{y}_{\text{new}}-({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}{y}_{\text{new}}-y-{x}^{2}y}_{⏟}}_{g({y}_{\text{new}})}=0.
$$

Therefore, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.5$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})={y}_{\text{new}}-({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}{y}_{\text{new}}-y-{x}^{2}y.
$$

$$
{y}^{′}=5{x}^{3}y,\,y(0)=1
$$

Using the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx=0.5,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step. Which of the following is the **general form** of $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ in terms of the new values ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and ${y}_{\text{new}},$ and the current values $x$ and $y?$
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In this example, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(5{x}^{3}y+5({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}{y}_{\text{new}})\cdot 0.5 \\  & =\frac{5}{4}{x}^{3}y+\frac{5}{4}({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{5}{4}{x}^{3}y+\frac{5}{4}({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}{y}_{\text{new}},\end{aligned}
$$

and moving all terms to the left-hand side gives the equation

$$
{{{y}_{\text{new}}-\frac{5}{4}({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}{y}_{\text{new}}-y-\frac{5}{4}{x}^{3}y}_{⏟}}_{g({y}_{\text{new}})}=0.
$$

Therefore, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.5$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})={y}_{\text{new}}-\frac{5}{4}({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}{y}_{\text{new}}-y-\frac{5}{4}{x}^{3}y.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=3x\sqrt{y},\,y(1)=1
$$

Using the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx=1,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step. Which of the following is the **specific function** $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ used in the first step?
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In this example, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3x\sqrt{y}+3{x}_{\text{new}}\sqrt{{y}_{\text{new}}})\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{3}{2}x\sqrt{y}+\frac{3}{2}{x}_{\text{new}}\sqrt{{y}_{\text{new}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{3}{2}x\sqrt{y}+\frac{3}{2}{x}_{\text{new}}\sqrt{{y}_{\text{new}}},\end{aligned}
$$

and moving all terms to the left-hand side gives the equation

$$
{y}_{\text{new}}-\frac{3}{2}{x}_{\text{new}}\sqrt{{y}_{\text{new}}}-y-\frac{3}{2}x\sqrt{y}=0.
$$

So, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=1$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})={y}_{\text{new}}-\frac{3}{2}{x}_{\text{new}}\sqrt{{y}_{\text{new}}}-y-\frac{3}{2}x\sqrt{y}.
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is

$$
{x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=1+1=2,
$$

Therefore, the function used in the first step is

$$
\begin{aligned}g({y}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{new}}-\frac{3}{2}(2)\sqrt{{y}_{\text{new}}}-1-\frac{3}{2}(1)\sqrt{1} \\  & ={y}_{\text{new}}-3\sqrt{{y}_{\text{new}}}-\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=x+2{y}^{2},\,y(0.5)=0
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step and Newton's method to approximate $y(1).$ Round your answer to two decimal places.

$y(1)≈$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

Since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=1,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=1-0.5=0.5.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((x+2{y}^{2})+({x}_{\text{new}}+2({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}))\cdot 0.5 \\  & =0.25x+0.5{y}^{2}+0.25{x}_{\text{new}}+0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+0.25x+0.5{y}^{2}+0.25{x}_{\text{new}}+0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

and moving all terms to the left-hand side gives the equation

$$
-0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-y-0.5{y}^{2}-0.25{x}_{\text{new}}-0.25x=0.
$$

So, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.5$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=-0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-y-0.5{y}^{2}-0.25{x}_{\text{new}}-0.25x.
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is

$$
{x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=0.5+0.5=1.
$$

Then, using the initial condition $y(0.5)=0,$ we have $x=0.5$ and $y=0,$ so

$$
\begin{aligned}g({y}_{\text{new}}) & =-0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-0-0.5(0)^{2}-0.25\cdot 1-0.25\cdot 0.5 \\  & =-0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-0.25-0.125 \\  & =-0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+{y}_{\text{new}}-0.375.\end{aligned}
$$

We use a root-finding method with starting point $y=0$ to solve $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.$ We'll use Newton's method:

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{g({y}_{\text{new}})}{{g}^{′}({y}_{\text{new}})}.
$$

Note that the derivative of $g$ is

$$
{g}^{′}({y}_{\text{new}})=-({y}_{\text{new}})+1.
$$

Therefore, our Newton's method iterative scheme is as follows:

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{-0.5(({y}_{\text{new}})_{n})^{2}+({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-0.375}{-({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}+1}.
$$

Applying several iterations of Newton's method starting with $y(0.5)=0,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}({y}_{\text{new}})_{1} & =0 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{2} & ≈0.375 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{3} & ≈0.4875 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{4} & ≈0.4998\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y(1)≈0.50,$ rounded to two decimal places.

questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=x{y}^{2}-2,\,y(0)=2.02
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step and Newton's method to approximate $y(0.5).$ Round your answer to two decimal places.

$y(0.5)≈$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

Since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=0.5,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=0.5-0=0.5.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((x{y}^{2}-2)+({x}_{\text{new}}({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-2))\cdot 0.5 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(x{y}^{2}+{x}_{\text{new}}({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-4)\cdot 0.5 \\  & =0.25x{y}^{2}+0.25{x}_{\text{new}}({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+0.25x{y}^{2}+0.25{x}_{\text{new}}({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-1,\end{aligned}
$$

and moving all terms to the left-hand side gives the equation

$$
0.25{x}_{\text{new}}({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+0.25x{y}^{2}+y-1-{y}_{\text{new}}=0.
$$

So, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=0.5$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.25{x}_{\text{new}}({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+0.25x{y}^{2}+y-1-{y}_{\text{new}}.
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is

$$
{x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=0+0.5=0.5.
$$

 Then, the function $g$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}g({y}_{\text{new}}) & =0.25(0.5)({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+0.25(0)(2.02)^{2}+2.02-1-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & =0.125({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+1.02-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & =0.125({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}-{y}_{\text{new}}+1.02.\end{aligned}
$$

We use a root-finding method with starting point $y=2.02$ to solve $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.$ We'll use Newton's method:

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{g({y}_{\text{new}})}{{g}^{′}({y}_{\text{new}})}.
$$

Note that the derivative of $g$ is

$$
{g}^{′}({y}_{\text{new}})=0.25({y}_{\text{new}})-1.
$$

Therefore, our Newton's method iterative scheme is as follows:

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{0.125(({y}_{\text{new}})_{n})^{2}-({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}+1.02}{0.25(({y}_{\text{new}})_{n})-1}.
$$

Applying several iterations of Newton's method starting with $y(0)=2.02,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}({y}_{\text{new}})_{1} & =2.02 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{2} & ≈1.030\,202 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{3} & ≈1.195\,146 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{4} & ≈1.199\,996\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y(0.5)≈1.20,$ rounded to two decimal places.
